stories.title: Masked settlers attack Palestinians and journalist during West Bank olive harvest
stories.summary: Dozens of masked settlers assaulted Palestinians near the village of Abu Falah during the annual olive harvest, setting fire to cars and olive trees. A local official reported 12 Palestinians injured, including four dual Palestinian‑American citizens, and a foreign journalist was also wounded. Witnesses said an American citizen named Majdi was struck with nail‑studded sticks, sustaining deep head injuries, and his elderly mother was also hurt.
stories.why: The incident illustrates escalating settler violence that threatens civilian safety and press freedom in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Record number of ship attacks reported in Strait of Hormuz this week
stories.summary: BBC Verify analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data shows twelve vessels were reported attacked between 5 and 11 October, the highest weekly total since the US‑Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week saw ten attacks, including six vessels struck on a single Sunday, a one‑day high, and four attacks reported so far this week. Industry data suggests the rise in incidents has slowed the recent recovery in oil shipments through the strait.
stories.why: The increase in attacks could disrupt the flow of oil and other goods through a critical global shipping chokepoint.

stories.title: India's forex reserves shed $60 billion in six weeks as RBI steps in to support rupee, one of Asia's worst-performing currencies this year
stories.summary: India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by nearly $60 billion in six weeks to $726.027 billion as of October 9, from a record high of $785.706 billion on September 4. The fall was largely attributed to the Reserve Bank of India’s intervention to support the rupee amid rising crude oil prices, higher US yields and sustained foreign investor outflows.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Houthi missile strike hits Aden presidential palace, five killed, 16 injured
stories.summary: A Houthi missile attack struck al‑Maashiq Palace, the presidential palace in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16, including site guards and civilian employees. Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al‑Eryani said the prime minister and other ministers were unharmed. The Houthis said the strike targeted what they called the “Saudi enemy’s military operations headquarters” in Aden.
stories.why: The attack highlights the continued danger to Yemen’s internationally‑recognised government amid the civil war.
stories.previousTitle: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
stories.previousSummary: Five people have been killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.
